title: SepDiff: Self-Encoding Parameter Diffusion for Learning Latent Semantics

problem.claim: Parameter diffusion models aim to model parameter spaces and handle continuous and discrete data.

gap.claim: Existing parameter diffusion models cannot learn high-level semantic representations from parameter spaces because static encoders cannot capture semantic changes in parameters.

contributions.claim: SepDiff is a parameter-space representation learning framework for obtaining parameter-wise latent semantics with progressive structures.
SepDiff uses a self-encoder to learn latent semantics directly from parameters and integrates it into a parameter diffusion model for observations with various formats.
SepDiff incorporates mutual information terms to promote disentanglement and capture meaningful latent semantics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report illustrating seven representation learning tasks through an expansion of the parameter diffusion model.
The authors report extensive quantitative experimental results demonstrating superior effectiveness for learning parameter representations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bayesian Flow Networks are presented as a unified approach for modeling parameter spaces through diffusion.
Existing parameter diffusion models are described as unable to learn high-level semantic representations because common encoders are static.
The limitation motivates learning semantic representations hidden in parameter spaces to characterize noisy data.
SepDiff introduces parameter-wise latent semantics through self-encoding, parameter diffusion integration, and mutual-information-based disentanglement.
The authors report seven representation learning tasks and extensive quantitative results supporting SepDiff's effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Static encoders may fail to represent semantic changes in parameter spaces.

interpretation.claim: Representation learning methods may need parameter-dependent or progressive encodings when semantics evolve across parameter states.

application.claim: For models whose parameters encode changing or noisy information, consider learning latent representations directly from parameters rather than only from observations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that direct parameter encoding is preferable for all model classes or observation formats.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The architecture and optimization details of the self-encoder and mutual-information terms are unspecified.
The relationship between the seven tasks and the reported effectiveness is unspecified.
